text:
alex: Heads-up — after the host driver update (nvidia-driver 560.14) our CI perf harness shows a regression on the arch-aware kernel path for long sequences. P95 up and KV-cache miss rate increased.

mian: Can you paste the numbers + config so we can triage? Which model/run?

alex: model=redwood/rlhf-1b, batch sizes tested 1..4, seq=1024, hw=h100, autotune snapshot=autotune-2026-03-15-09
perf summary:
- p50: 58ms -> 72ms
- p95: 135ms -> 182ms
- kv cache miss rate: 2.1% -> 10.3%
log snippet:
```text
[2026-03-15T09:12:01Z] kernel_selector: chosen_path=vectorized_large_seq, score_delta=+0.22
[2026-03-15T09:12:01Z] kv_cache: eviction_rate +0.08, prefetch_miss +0.06
```

tian: Looks like the selector shifted from the shortseq fastpath to the large-seq vectorized path on the same inputs. Could be heuristic weight changes after the driver upgrade (scheduling/warp behavior).

ops-bot: Deploy bot: driver-upgrade-prod -> hostpool/h100-1 at 2026-03-15T09:10:22Z

mian: Can we repro on canary? If yes, we should either rollback the driver or force the previous selector heuristic while we diagnose.

alex: Reproduced on canary. Proposed immediate actions:
1) Canary rollback of driver on 10% of hosts.
2) Pin kernel selector heuristic to previous version (config flag).
3) Disable autotuner re-learning for affected pools for 24h.
4) Add KV-cache telemetry (evict rate, prefetch hits) and a regression alert.
Thoughts?

jen: +1. Ops can do the rollback. We need a runbook with exact commands and a correlation id for metrics. @ops-bot, please open a rollback ticket and start canary.

ops-bot: Rollback ticket created: RB-3482. Started canary rollback on h100-canary-2. Commands executed:
```bash
# rollback driver on canary node
ssh node-h100-canary-2 "sudo apt-get install nvidia-driver-560.12 -y && sudo systemctl restart nvidia-persistenced"
# pin kernel selector heuristic
redwoodctl set-config runtime.kernel_selector.heuristic_version=2026-03-01
```

tian: Also propose a temporary batching tweak for the affected hostpool: reduce max continuous batching cap to reduce KV-cache churn (cap 8 -> 4). Example config change (applied via config API):
```json
{"runtime": {"batching": {"max_continuous_batch_size": 4}}}
```

mian: Make sure all metrics are tagged with correlation id RB-3482 and create an alert: trigger page if p95 > baseline*1.10 for 10 min.

alex: I'll add a quick CI smoke that runs a short perf check after any driver bump to catch these flips early. Also adding an autotune safety-net ticket for versioned kernel profiles.

tian: Long-term fix: versioned kernel profiles tied to (driver, cuda, arch) so selector can fallback deterministically to a previously good profile per model/host-arch. Also checkpoint autotune state and make roll-forward opt-in.

jen: Postmortem owners: alex + tian. Ops will own rollback execution until pool restored.

alex: I'll update RB-3482 with the perf diffs and the canary plan. Keeping thread open until canary stabilizes.

ops-bot: Canary rollback completed on h100-canary-2 at 2026-03-15T09:24:29Z. Observed p95 revert: 182ms -> 128ms. KV miss rate back to ~2.4%.

alex: Nice. Do we want one more canary or roll full pool?

mian: One more canary then full rollback. Schedule in 30m.

jen: Also document the temporary kernel_selector pin and batching tweak as short-lived mitigations in the ticket.

alex: On it. Closing loop once full rollback done.
